Dose (S)equence (C)omparison Rate

Source: R/sc_rate.R
sc_rate.Rd

This function checks, for each person, whether the doses they received of an ordered dose sequence (e.g. DTP1, DTP2 and DTP3) are consistent, and calculates the percentage of consistent and inconsistent sequences, further disaggregating by geographic level of residence, using data from the electronic immunization registry (EIR).

Usage

sc_rate(
  data.EIR,
  vaccines,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  aggregated = TRUE,
  birth_cohorts = NULL,
  allow_same_day = FALSE,
  fix_residence = TRUE
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See immunABC.EIR for expected structure.

vaccines

Character. A character vector of at least two doses with the ordered dose sequence to evaluate, e.g. c("DTP1", "DTP2", "DTP3").

geo_level

Character. The geographic level to aggregate results by. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0".

aggregated

Logical. Whether to pool all inconsistent sequences into a single INCONSISTENT category (TRUE, default), or keep CONSISTENT as a single category and show every inconsistent combination of doses received (FALSE), e.g. "DTP1 + DTP3", flagging the ones administered out of chronological order (e.g. "DTP1 + DTP2 (out of order)").

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) for which the rate should be calculated. If NULL (default), all available cohorts are used.

allow_same_day

Logical. Whether two consecutive doses administered on the same day are considered chronologically consistent. Default is FALSE, since doses of the same vaccine series should not be administered on the same day.

fix_residence

Logical. When a person's residence differs across their records, whether to correct all of that person's records to the residence of their most recent vaccination (TRUE, default) or leave the data as-is (FALSE), in which case each person is assigned the residence of their first record.

Value

A data frame with one row per sequence category for the specified geo_level, with the following columns:

  • sequence: the category of each sequence, one of:

    • CONSISTENT: no dose skipped and every dose administered in chronological order.

    • INCONSISTENT (only when aggregated = TRUE): a dose was skipped and/or administered out of chronological order. When aggregated = FALSE, inconsistent sequences are shown as the combination of doses received, e.g. "DTP1 + DTP3" (missing DTP2), with the suffix " (out of order)" when the doses were not administered in chronological order.

    • DATE_MISSING: no dose skipped and no chronological inconsistency found, but at least one dose received has no date_vax, so the chronological order cannot be fully evaluated.

  • consistent: whether that category corresponds to a consistent sequence (NA for DATE_MISSING).

  • n: number of people in that category.

  • total: total number of people with at least one dose of the sequence.

  • rate: percentage of people in that category (n / total * 100).

Details

A sequence is consistent when both of the following hold:

  • No earlier dose is skipped, i.e. the doses received are the first doses of the sequence. For a DTP1, DTP2, DTP3 sequence, "DTP1", "DTP1 + DTP2" and "DTP1 + DTP2 + DTP3" pass this check (the person may simply not have finished the sequence yet), while "DTP2", "DTP3", "DTP1 + DTP3" and "DTP2 + DTP3" do not.

  • The doses received were administered in chronological order, i.e. each dose after the previous dose received in the sequence (e.g. DTP2 after DTP1).

Only people with at least one dose of the sequence are evaluated. Since this is a nominal indicator, each person is assigned to a single place of residence (see fix_residence).
